observations: Photo 0 shows a used inline diesel engine with red-painted valve covers, alternator, drive belts, and intake piping visible.
Photo 1 shows the top of the same engine with injector lines, rocker cover, and exhaust manifold.
Photo 2 shows a side angle of the engine block, mounting points, and hose connections.
No brand badge, model plate, or casting number is legible in any photo.
A watermark reads 'POSTED ON JUMIA CHARLES UMEH' across all three photos.

claims.claim: The engine is from an Iveco Eurocargo
claims.evidence: No Iveco or Eurocargo badge or plate visible in photos 0-2.

claims.claim: It is a Tector 5 or Tector 7 diesel engine
claims.evidence: No Tector, Iveco, or model designation visible on the engine in photos 0-2.
Seller wording only; no photo shows vehicle application or cargo truck context.

risks.risk: Engine does not run or turn over
risks.proof: Video of the engine cranking and running, or at least turning by hand or starter.

risks.risk: Engine is not an Iveco Tector but a different make or model
risks.proof: Clear photo of the engine identification plate or block stamping.
risks.if_unproven: as a generic diesel engine of unknown origin

risks.risk: Internal damage such as low compression, knock, or overheating
risks.proof: Compression test results or video of engine running under load.

risks.risk: Missing components such as turbocharger, injectors, ECU, or ancillaries
risks.proof: Photo showing the complete engine with all components attached.

proof_requests: Clear photo of any engine identification plate, VIN stamp, or casting number on the block.
Video of the engine cranking and running.
Photo showing the full engine with turbo, injectors, and all ancillaries present.
response.reason: The photos show a used diesel engine; even if the Iveco Tector claim is unproven and the engine is untested, it can be priced at worst case as a non-running engine core of unknown make.
